projects.name: L-STAR
projects.description: I developed a workflow that uses visual LLM comparisons to select spatial domain detection methods and combine their clusterings into a consensus tissue partition.
highlights: Developed the L-STAR visual LLM workflow for spatial domain detection, with structured prompts, repeated comparisons of spatial maps and optional histology, JSON logs, and win-rate-based method selection.

Implemented consensus clustering with co-assignment matrices and average linkage. Added an all-wise comparison mode that aggregates repeated rankings to select ensemble members with one LLM call per repeat.

Designed comparative experiments across six spatial transcriptomics datasets to examine ensemble size, alternative LLMs, and fixed-method consensus baselines, separating the roles of method selection and clustering aggregation.

Built marker-gene-based domain annotation with spot- and cell-level labels and an Unknown option. Evaluated agreement with manual annotations using BioLORD-2023 embeddings and within-dataset permutation tests.

Audited sensitivity to color palettes, presentation order, and redundant candidate methods by examining ranking agreement, selected-method overlap, and clustering stability through repeated runs and controlled perturbations.

projects.name: TRACE
projects.description: I developed TRACE, an end-to-end LangGraph workflow for single-cell and spatial pseudotime analysis, implemented in the pseudotime-agent package.
highlights: Developed pseudotime-agent, an end-to-end LangGraph package coordinating Python, R/Seurat, and LLM inference for single-cell and spatial pseudotime analysis. Implemented schema validation, corrective retries, provenance tracking, and fingerprint-validated replay with support for expert-supplied inputs.

Designed parallel UMAP and t-SNE workflows for cell-type annotation, lineage-family adjudication, and cross-embedding trajectory fusion, using assay-aware molecular evidence for scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq inputs.

Designed LLM-guided spatial process-instance resolution using molecular profiles and tissue topology to distinguish repeated local processes within connected tissue, with explicit cell membership, local seeds, and unresolved assignments.

Implemented expression-weighted graph pseudotime with instance-level ordering review and partial-trajectory support. Separated molecular lineage hypotheses, physical feasibility, and spatial evidence in auditable execution rules.

Built an optional completion module with evidence-based assignment review and donor-restricted imputation. Preserved original inference outputs and unresolved multi-instance assignments, keeping graph-derived and imputed values distinct.

Designed and implemented bPOS, an exact branch-aware pseudotime metric that jointly evaluates lineage membership and within-lineage ordering using scalable block processing and inclusion-exclusion counting.

Diagnosed a bug in the dyneval-based benchmark evaluation of F1branches. Reimplemented the published Jaccard, recovery, relevance, and harmonic-mean definition over the full cell scope and added diagnostic comparisons.

Built reproducible comparisons with Monocle 3, Slingshot, and TSCAN. Designed synthetic negative controls, perturbation tests, and staged replay experiments to assess spatial assumptions, instance partitioning, and pseudotime stability.

projects.name: Med2State
projects.description: I am designing Med2State, a framework for learning structured patient-state representations from incomplete multimodal health records, building on the implemented Med2Vec+ prototype.
highlights: Designing Med2State, a framework for learning structured patient-state representations from incomplete multimodal health records, with configurable evidence encoders and disease, procedure, and treatment channels.

Formulating partial-evidence learning with longitudinal context. Planning concept-readout, similar-state retrieval, and trajectory evaluations to assess semantic content and missing-input behavior before validating downstream use.

Implemented Med2Vec+, the note-aware PyTorch prototype underlying this research direction, with multi-aspect patient histories, demographic covariates, and visit-aligned BioClinicalBERT note embeddings.
Designed multi-head cross-attention to condition EHR embeddings on clinical notes. Built Med2Vec-compatible input and output interfaces and component-ablation workflows for the prototype.

projects.name: PaperEval
projects.description: I built data pipelines and LLM-based workflows for acceptance prediction, manuscript assessment, and review-response evaluation.
highlights: Built Selenium and asynchronous data-collection pipelines for major machine-learning conferences on OpenReview, storing papers, reviews, scores, author responses, and metadata in JSON with resumable checkpoints.
Extracted author contact information from conference PDFs with PyMuPDF to enrich OpenReview metadata.

Fine-tuned GPT-4o for acceptance prediction using progressively richer inputs: paper metadata, reviewer scores, and review comments. Implemented training-data preparation and classification evaluation workflows.

Developed LLM-based agent workflows for manuscript and figure assessment, review-response scoring, and response generation. Evaluated generated responses against author replies from accepted and rejected submissions.
Designed a bounded Gaussian-noise mapping to convert acceptance levels into continuous constructiveness targets.

projects.name: MUDAC 2025
projects.description: I developed features and models for sparse, high-dimensional numerical and text data in the Midwest Undergraduate Data Analysis Competition.
highlights: Encoded sparse, high-dimensional numerical and text data with embeddings, sentiment scores, and pairwise similarities.
Applied Cox proportional hazards regression and a causal Bayesian network to study match duration and closure.
Designed a mixture-of-experts model with regression, MLP, and Transformer experts for different feature types and a learned gating network. Compared it with random forest and XGBoost baselines.
Placed 7th in Innovation & Creativity.

projects.name: Public Health Equity Data Challenge
projects.description: I analyzed questionnaire data on inequities in access to mental-health resources and co-authored the analysis report and poster.
highlights: Analyzed Hennepin County questionnaire data on inequities in access to mental-health resources using multiple regression, ridge regression, decision trees, and causal inference methods.
Built a mental-health prediction interface in tkinter backed by an AdaBoost model in scikit-learn.
Co-authored the analysis report and poster and placed in the top 25% of the undergraduate division.

projects.name: Overlapping Group LASSO
projects.description: I compared overlapping group LASSO implementations and implemented an optimized algorithm in C for integration with R.
highlights: Compared overlapping_LeastR from the MATLAB SLEP library with oglasso in the R package VennLasso under matched problem sizes and convergence tolerances.
Simulated 1,000 large sparse-matrix datasets with overlapping groups and compared runtime using t-tests.
Implemented the optimized algorithm in C for integration with R.
